title: Camp 2 close: the camel kneels
hook: he reaches Yathrib, where his camel kneels on a plot of land, a mosque is built, and the calendar begins again

segments.voice: Yesterday, the cave of Thawr and the trackers at its mouth. Your line was Allah is with us. Did you whisper it anywhere? Today, the last day of the stories. Day ninety-six.

For days, the people of Yathrib have been walking out to the edge of town every morning, watching the road from Mecca in the heat, and going home disappointed. Then one day a lookout shouts: he's here. The whole town pours out. First he stops at Quba, just outside, and builds a simple mosque there, the first in Islam. Then he rides into the town itself, and everyone wants him. Clan after clan grabs his camel's reins: stay with us, stay with us. And he says, gently: let her go. She is under orders. And the camel, al-Qaswa', walks on through the streets, while the whole town follows her, holding its breath.
screen: `EVERY MORNING, WATCHING THE ROAD.` → `QUBA: THE FIRST MOSQUE.` → `LET HER GO. SHE IS UNDER ORDERS.`

segments.voice: Ibn Ishaq and Sahih al-Bukhari both tell where she stopped. The camel knelt on an open yard where dates were laid out to dry. It belonged to two orphan boys. The boys wanted to give it to him as a gift; he insisted on paying them for it. There, with his own hands, carrying bricks alongside everyone else, he built the mosque that, rebuilt and enlarged many times, still stands at the heart of the city. Yathrib got a new name: Madinat an-Nabi, the city of the Prophet, or simply al-Madinah, the city. The people who had come from Mecca were the muhajirun, the emigrants. The people of Medina who took them in were the ansar, the helpers. And years later, the Muslims began counting their calendar from this year, six hundred and twenty-two. Not from his birth, not from the cave. From the hijra. The year a community began. And that is where the stories end, for now. Look how far you've come. Seventy-four days ago, on day twenty-two, you met Adam, the steward the angels questioned. Then Iblis who would not bow, and the garden with its one tree. Two sons. Nuh building on dry land. Ibrahim and the idols, the fire made cool, Hajar running between the hills, the House raised. Musa in a basket on the river, the fire on the mountain, the sea. Yusuf, from the well to no blame on you today. Maryam, Zakariyya and Yahya, Isa by Allah's leave. Yunus in three darknesses. And then the Prophet ﷺ himself: an orphan in the desert, a trusted young man, a cave, one word, read, and a road out of Mecca. You know these stories now. Tomorrow, camp three begins: the practices, how Muslims actually pray and live it.
screen: `THE CAMEL KNEELS ON AN ORPHANS' YARD.` · `YATHRIB BECOMES AL-MADINAH.` · `THE CALENDAR BEGINS AGAIN.` · `FROM ADAM TO THE HIJRA.` · then, large: `YOU KNOW THESE STORIES NOW.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: list the prophets you now know. Settle, and breathe. Then, slowly, name them to yourself, one per breath. Adam. Nuh. Ibrahim. Isma'il. Musa. Yusuf. Zakariyya. Yahya. Isa. Yunus. Muhammad ﷺ. Add any others you remember. With each name, let one picture come: a boat, a fire, a well, a palm tree, a fish, a cave. If you pray, you can add, peace be upon them. Notice how many you carry now. The bell holds the time.
Camp two, closed. Khalifah, Iblis, waswas, tawbah, khalil, Zamzam, Ka'ba, sabr jamil, nafs, Isa, yatim, amanah, iqra, Hijra: the stories of the prophets, and then the Prophet.
Your line: you know these stories now. Today, tell one of them to someone, in your own words. Tomorrow, camp three opens with the intention behind every prayer. Day ninety-six.

howItsDone: Muslims date the Islamic year from the Hijra, and many visit the Prophet's Mosque in Medina, which stands on the land where his camel knelt; the first of Muharram marks the Islamic new year.

fork.setup: the Prophet rides into Yathrib, and every clan grabs his camel's reins, begging him to stay with them. what does he do?
options: let the camel go where she's led.
fork.reveal: let her go, she is under orders: the camel knelt on the orphans' yard, and the mosque was built there (Ibn Ishaq; Bukhari).

original.note: Arabic: the city; short for Madinat an-Nabi, the city of the Prophet.

trapdoor: what you thought: he arrived in Medina.
what it means: a hunted man arrived in a town that had waited for him, let a camel choose where to build, paid two orphans for the land, and a community began.
what a scholar hears: the Hijri calendar was set under 'Umar, counting year one from the Hijra rather than the birth or the first revelation.

sources.ref: Sahih al-Bukhari 3906 (the arrival; the orphans' land; building the mosque)
Ibn Ishaq, Sirat Rasul Allah (Quba; 'let her go, she is under orders'; al-Qaswa')
sources.work: Sirat Rasul Allah (Ibn Ishaq, via Ibn Hisham)

sources.ref: Qur'an 9:108 (a mosque founded on duty from the first day, often read as Quba)

notes: Details from Bukhari 3906 and Ibn Ishaq (the lookouts, Quba, the reins, the orphans Sahl and Suhayl, paying for the land). Hadith number from memory; confirm.
The Hijri calendar was instituted under 'Umar (c. 638); stated as 'years later'. Confirm.

The word-segment list of camp two's words draws on the index words for days 22–95 that are real words (khalifah, Iblis, waswas, tawbah, khalil, Zamzam, Ka'ba, sabr jamil, nafs, Isa, yatim, amanah, iqra, Hijra). Confirm against the final index.
The practice lists prophets met on this path; Muslims also honor others (Hud, Salih, Lut, Dawud, Sulayman, and more). The listener is invited to add them.
'The first mosque in Islam' for Quba: the common view; confirm.

Audit 2026-09-30: 'seventy-five days ago, on day twenty-two' corrected to seventy-four; the Prophet's Mosque is now described as rebuilt and enlarged many times, not as the same building still standing.
